decisions.option: Owner answer 2026-10-05: the privacy page states plainly that no personally identifiable information is collected and all responses are anonymous; no controller name or contact shown.
decisions.what_changed: Both privacy notices (static PRIVACY_SECTIONS, server SERVER_PRIVACY_SECTIONS) lose every TODO(user) placeholder and the 'Who runs this site' section; a new first section 'In short' says it plainly. Static: adds a true line about what the web host sees; the online-version section no longer carries draft terms. Server: retention, legal basis, region and deletion are written as facts true of the server as built (24 months is stated as the plan; backups and archive named). TERMS_VERSION and TERMS_VERSION_SERVER bumped (no SQL names a terms version), so consent is asked again. Comments in Privacy.svelte and both copy files no longer mention TODO(user). New tests fail on 'TODO' in any exported copy string and in rendered pages (static and server).

strings.before: Controller: TODO(user): name of the person or organisation responsible for this site.
strings.after: (static) HumanBench collects no personally identifiable information, and all responses are anonymous. It never asks for your name, your email address or anything else that identifies you, and there are no accounts.

strings.before: Contact: TODO(user): an email address for questions and requests about your data.
strings.after: (static) In this version your answers stay on your device. They leave it only if you share them yourself, for example by sending someone your save file.
The web host that serves these pages sees your network address when your browser loads them, as every web host does. It never receives your answers.

strings.before: An online version may send your answers to a server to improve the questions. It would ask for your consent again and this notice would be updated first.
strings.after: An online version may send your answers to a server to improve the questions. Before it does, this notice will be updated and you will be asked for your consent again.

strings.before: Draft terms for that version, to be confirmed: TODO(user): retention period (draft: 24 months), legal basis (draft: consent), and where the data is held.
strings.after: The plan for that version is the same: no name and no email address, answers stored only under a random identifier, and answers kept for at most 24 months.

strings.before: (server) Controller: TODO(user): name of the person or organisation responsible for this site. / Contact: TODO(user): an email address for questions and requests about your data.
strings.after: (server, one paragraph) HumanBench collects no personally identifiable information, and all responses are anonymous. It never asks for your name, your email address or anything else that identifies you, and there are no accounts. Your answers are stored under a random identifier, not under who you are.

strings.before: (server) Draft terms, to be confirmed: TODO(user): retention period (draft: 24 months), legal basis (draft: consent), and where the data is held (draft: a region the user chooses, in the EU or the US).
strings.after: Your answers are kept because you agreed to it on the first screen: your consent is the basis. The plan is to keep them for at most 24 months and then delete them. They are held by a database hosting provider in the European Union or the United States.

strings.before: (server) You can ask for everything stored for your identifier to be deleted at any time, on the page “Your data on the server”, with your recovery phrase or a save file the server issued. Deleting from the server does not touch the save files you downloaded or what this browser holds.
strings.after: You can delete everything stored on the server for your identifier at any time, on the page “Your data on the server”, with your recovery phrase or a save file the server issued. It is removed from the database at once, and from the encrypted weekly backups within eight weeks. Answers of sessions older than 30 days are also copied, without your identifier, into an encrypted archive used to improve the questions, and deleting does not reach that archive. Deleting from the server does not touch the save files you downloaded or what this browser holds.

deviations: DESIGN §13 asks the notice to name the controller ('controller = you'); by the owner's answer it names none. Purpose, retention (24 months), legal basis (consent) and deletion are still covered.
open_issues: 'No personally identifiable information' and 'anonymous' are true in the everyday sense, not in the strict GDPR sense DESIGN §13 itself cites (Recital 26: a random id linked to responses is pseudonymous personal data). The server variant also keeps, for about two days, a salted hash of the network address for rate limits, and its hosting provider logs network addresses; the notice says both right after, so no sentence is false, but a plain claim without them would be untrue for the server variant. The static notice now says the web host (GitHub Pages) sees the network address on page load.

Server notice states 24-month retention as 'the plan': supabase/README.md says the 24-month purge of database rows is not built and the archive expiry (hb db nightly --expire-archive-days 730) is off unless the owner turns it on. Build/turn these on before any data-collecting deploy (M2.6), then the sentence can drop 'The plan is'.
The server's 'Report a problem' note is free text; a person could type personal details into it despite the request not to.
DATA_DELETE_TEXT on the data page ('This deletes every session and the backup stored for an identifier') does not mention the backups and the archive the notice now names; see requests.

decisions.option: Owner answer 2026-10-05: tell the person in advance to have scratch paper and a pencil ready, and not to use calculators or LLMs.
decisions.what_changed: Honour screen: HONOUR_TEXT kept word for word; a new paragraph under it (HONOUR_TOOLS) allows paper and pencil, rules out a calculator or an AI chatbot, and says screen readers, zoom and other accessibility settings are fine (the owner's 'assistive technology' is not used, since in accessibility it means screen readers). The Quantitative interstitial blurb no longer contradicts it.

strings.after: You may want scratch paper and a pencil ready: writing things down is allowed. Please do not use a calculator or an AI chatbot. Screen readers, zoom and other accessibility settings are fine to use.

strings.before: Solve short number problems and type your answer. Keep paper and a calculator out of reach.
strings.after: Solve short number problems and type your answer. Scratch paper and a pencil are fine; please do not use a calculator or an AI chatbot.

deviations: Wording says 'AI chatbot' rather than 'LLM' (plainer; same meaning) and adds that accessibility tools are fine, so 'no AI tools' is not read as 'no screen reader'.

decisions.what_changed: segments.ts gains needsSight(what), built from INTERSTITIAL_SKIP so it names the interstitial's own button, appended to the RT and Spatial blurbs. Option B (an 'assistive' RT input type) skipped: it needs its own norms (§13 'the mode is stored and normed separately'), which wait for the norming work.

strings.before: A target appears on the screen. Respond as fast as you can once you see it. A few practice trials come first.
strings.after: A target appears on the screen. Respond as fast as you can once you see it. A few practice trials come first. This part needs you to see the screen. If you use a screen reader or cannot see the target, choose “Skip this part”: it will show as not measured.

strings.before: Turn objects in your mind. Decide which option is the same object as the target, rotated.
strings.after: Turn objects in your mind. Decide which option is the same object as the target, rotated. This part needs you to see the screen. If you use a screen reader or cannot see the figures, choose “Skip this part”: it will show as not measured.

strings.after: Short tasks of reasoning, memory and speed. Your results are shown as a profile with ranges, not as a single score.
